doc.title: Barry Kernfeld interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 16, 2020

title: Whether being a musician drove his concern with accuracy
summary: He says being a musician helped him judge writing about music, but his nerdy intellectual side drives the insistence on truth about influence.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Do you think that the fact that you’re a musician contributed to the fact that this is so important to you?

Sure. I’m not sure how to answer that question. I mean I was obsessed with jazz, so interesting question. I’m pausing here to think that the reason it’s so important to me may have — I think the fact that I was a musician had a lot to do with Grove and my ability to write about music and decide if comments about the music were B.S. or not. But I think what you just asked has more to do with me being a kind of nerdy intellectual. And that it was important to me for those reasons, because there is to my mind this obsession in jazz with precedents. And if you’re going to talk about precedents, who did what, who influenced whom, then you have to make sure it’s based on truth and not on error.
